newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England deals at unchanged interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England deals at unchanged interest rates.

text.p: The Bank of England appeared to have left official interest rates unchanged on Wednesday after the monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
The Bank set an unchanged repo rate of 6.0 percent for its routine money market operations at midday.

However, as the meeting ended only just before the Bank conducted its midday operations, traders said it was possible a change in interest rates could be signalled in the next round of operations at around 1430 GMT.
Clarke sets interest rates after taking advice from the Bank of England, but the central bank normally makes no formal announcement if rates are left unchanged.
George has recently been pressing for a rise of a quarter of a percentage point in interest rates because he fears a resurgence in inflation.
But Clarke, whose Conservative government faces an election in the next two months, has rejected his advice, arguing that there is no clear evidence that the economy is about to overheat.
Clarke has a strong political incentive not to raise rates before the election as this would mean dearer home loans for millions of Britons.
